evidence: Cic. Phil. 2.32: num conturbō tē? (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To throw someone’s mind into disorder; also simply “upset, worry” (Cic. Att. 7.2.2).
Of plans, ranks, a household or a mind: to throw everything into disorder.

terms.gloss: be at a loss, be stuck
terms.comment: “I’m confused, I’m stuck” is haereō: not knowing what to say or do. Its first sense is “stick, cling”.
Properly “pour together, mix” (see mix); of the mind, “perplex”, mostly after Augustus (Lewis & Short). Taking one thing for another is not cōnfundere but a mistake (see mistake).

evidence: Cic. N. D. 1.3: perturbātiō et cōnfūsiō vītae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A noun for the state: classically cōnfūsiō is a confounding or disorder (Cic.; Lewis & Short); Andresian adds animī.

phrases.english: I’m not confusing you, am I?

phrases.latin: haerēbat nebulō: quō sē verteret, nōn habēbat
phrases.english: the scoundrel was stuck: he had no idea which way to turn
